CT-201.title: Invalid pallet lines are slipping through
CT-201.text: Atlas Ridge’s billing team found that some obviously invalid freight lines are still being accepted in load planning instead of being rejected. For shipment TW-61427, a bad pallet line with no usable footprint was processed without error, and another edge-case line at the trailer limit also made it through when it should have been blocked. This matters because those shipments can then be rated and billed off bad freight data.

comments.text: Triage: confirmed against the linear-feet policy. Pallet count must be positive and anything over a 53' trailer must be rejected. TW-61427 was submitted as PalletLine(0) and produced linear_feet_for_shipment = 0 instead of an error; the at-trailer-limit line was likewise not blocked. Please add regression tests for zero/invalid footprint and over-length loads.

CT-202.title: Linehaul premium rate is off on a multi-premium load
CT-202.text: Carrier billing is showing a slightly inflated linehaul rate on a load where multiple accessorial premiums should stack cleanly. Load TW-58213 was rated with hazmat, team service, and an overweight permit, and the per-mile linehaul amount came out higher than expected, which will ripple into the settlement total. Please review this before more loads with the same combination are invoiced.

comments.text: Triage: confirmed. Per the rate-per-mile policy, 300 mi with hazmat + team + overweight = 2.20 + 0.18 + 0.22 + 0.10 = $2.70/mi (team applies only over 250 mi). TW-58213 computed 2.71, one cent high. Likely a threshold/stacking issue; add a regression test at 300 mi with all three premiums.

CT-203.title: Produce load not getting seal requirement at threshold
CT-203.text: Hartline's ops team flagged a produce load that should have required a seal, but the dispatch record shows it as not required. This matters because their drivers and yard staff rely on the seal flag before the load leaves the shipper, and a missing seal requirement can create a food-safety compliance issue. Please check the seal requirement decision for this shipment.

comments.text: Triage: P1 because a missing seal is a food-safety/compliance exposure at dispatch. Per the seal policy, fresh produce requires a seal at 10,000 lb or more (Hartline Retail also at 5+ pallets). This reads like an off-by-one at the threshold. Please check the exact-threshold case and add boundary regression tests for produce weight and Hartline pallet count.

Fixed off-by-one threshold: PRODUCE_WEIGHT_THRESHOLD changed from 10001 to 10000 so fresh produce at exactly 10,000 lb requires a seal. Added boundary regression tests for produce weight (10,000 vs 9,999.99) and Hartline pallets (5.0 vs 4.9). Full suite passes: 226 passed.

CT-204.title: Tender expiry is wrong for weekend offers
CT-204.text: Ops flagged a couple of customer tenders where the offer expiration looks off when the tender is sent on a Friday evening or over the weekend. One Chicago-area load was offered after business hours on Friday and another on Saturday, but both are expiring too early instead of carrying through to the next business day. This is causing dispatch to lose valid offers before the customer has a chance to review them.

comments.text: Triage: confirmed. Per the tender-expiry policy, a Friday 6:00 PM or Saturday tender starts Monday at 7:00 AM carrier local time and runs 2 business hours, expiring Monday 9:00 AM local (then converted to UTC). Current results expire too early. Add regression tests for Friday-evening and Saturday tenders across a weekend.

Fixed in tender_expiry.py: _is_business_day treated Saturday (weekday 5) as a business day, so Friday-evening and Saturday tenders expired Saturday instead of carrying to Monday. Now weekdays 0-4 only. Added regression tests for Friday 18:00 and Saturday 10:00 Chicago offers, both expiring Monday 09:00 local. Full suite: 224 passed. PR opened.

CT-205.title: Reefer excursion stays open across a logger gap
CT-205.text: Arctic Rail's ops team is seeing a reefer excursion carry on through a long logger gap instead of ending with the last reading before the break. For load TW-58213, the unit was back in range after the gap, but the excursion on the monitor still appears to run through the missing period and closes later than it should. That makes the temperature event look longer and fully closed when it should not.

comments.text: Triage: confirmed. Per the reefer rules, if the logger is quiet more than 15 minutes while out of range, the excursion ends at the last reading received and is marked not closed. TW-58213 currently runs the excursion through the gap and closes later. Add a regression test with a >15-minute logger gap while out of range.

Fixed. The gap check in `_out_of_range_runs` only ran while no run was open (and appended `None` to the run list), so an in-progress excursion never ended at a logger gap. Now a gap > 15 minutes while out of range closes the run at its last received reading with closed=False; exactly 15 minutes does not split. Regression tests added (long gap while out of range; 15-minute boundary). Full suite green: 224 passed. PR opened for review.

CT-206.title: Bridge axle span violation missing on tandem group
CT-206.text: Ops flagged TW-58213 because the axle-weight check is missing a bridge-law violation on one of the recent tandems. The truck is being released as compliant even though the axle group looks too heavy for the span between the steer axle and the rear tandem set, so this could let an overweight unit leave the yard without a warning. Please take a look at the axle-weight review for this load before it is used in dispatch.

comments.text: Triage: confirmed defect. Federal bridge/span limits apply to every group of two or more consecutive axles, in addition to single-axle (20,000), tandem (34,000), and gross (80,000) checks. The special double-tandem allowance (34,000 each) applies only when the outer axles are >= 36 ft apart. Evaluate the bridge weight formula using the span and axle count for the steer-plus-rear-tandem group on TW-58213; a group over the formula must be flagged as a separate bridge/span violation. Add a regression test with a tandem group that exceeds the bridge limit. P1, safety/compliance. Also first in the Hartline go-live chain.

CT-207.title: EDI 997 ack marked accepted despite overage discrepancy
CT-207.text: Ops noticed one 997 acknowledgement on a recent interchange that looks wrong in our portal: the document was accepted even though the counts don’t reconcile cleanly. For interchange EDI-77491, the trading partner’s included set appears to have more entries than what we actually processed, so this should not have been treated as a clean acceptance. Please review the acknowledgement status logic for this case because it affects how we flag mismatches for downstream auditing.

comments.text: Triage: confirmed on EDI-77491. Counts are accepted=9950, rejected=0, included=10000, so the overage is 50 transaction sets. With overage tolerance 0.0049 (49/10000), 50 exceeds the allowed overage, so the result must be COUNT_MISMATCH, not ACCEPTED. Control numbers match (77/77), so CONTROL_MISMATCH does not apply. Fix the tolerance comparison (overage vs tolerated amount) and add a regression test at this boundary (50 over included, tolerance 0.0049). Part of the Hartline chain, blocked by CT-206.

CT-208.title: OR road use tax looks doubled on long-haul mileage
CT-208.text: Our billing team found a road use tax discrepancy on an Oregon haul tied to load TW-58213. The tax amount is coming out much higher than expected for a standard loaded-mile move just over the long-haul threshold, which is throwing off settlement and could overbill the customer on state road use charges. Please take a look before we release the next batch.

comments.text: Triage: confirmed defect. Road-use tax: taxable miles = loaded + empty (yard and ferry ignored, exempt miles reduce taxable, cannot exceed road miles). De minimis if taxable < 10 (no tax/surcharge). For taxable miles over 1,000 apply a 2% bulk filing discount to the base tax before any surcharge; round to nearest cent half-up. Electric surcharge only when taxable >= 100. The doubled result on TW-58213 suggests miles or the discount/surcharge are being applied twice or the discount is being applied as a multiplier. Add a regression test just over the 1,000-mile threshold. P1 (customer overbilling). Second in the Hartline chain, blocked by CT-207.

Triage: CT-207 is done, so this blocker is cleared — CT-208 is now the head of the Hartline chain and ready to work. Rules: taxable miles = loaded + empty (yard and ferry ignored, exempt miles reduce, cannot exceed road miles). De minimis if taxable < 10 (no tax/surcharge). For taxable miles over 1,000, apply a 2% bulk filing discount to the base tax before any surcharge. Round to nearest cent half-up. Electric surcharge only when taxable >= 100. A doubled TW-58213 result suggests miles or the discount/surcharge applied twice, or the discount applied as a multiplier. Add a regression test just over the 1,000-mile threshold.

CT-209.title: Drayage hazmat conversion is rounding up one basis point
CT-209.text: Ops noticed a hazmat truckload moving into drayage is being converted with a slightly higher factor than expected. The load looks like it picked up the drayage uplift on top of the hazmat adjustment, which is causing the converted value to come out a hair high and is throwing off settlement review for this customer. Please check the conversion result on TW-58213.

comments.text: Triage: confirmed defect. For a hazmat truckload->drayage conversion, hazmat gets the smaller drayage uplift; do not stack the full hazmat adjustment on top of the drayage uplift. Final factor rounded to four decimals half-up and never below 0.2500. Verify the conversion result on TW-58213 and add a regression test for hazmat + drayage. Note: CT-212 is another drayage conversion discrepancy in the same module; check whether both share a root cause. Third in the Hartline chain, blocked by CT-208.

Triage: no separate PR needed. CT-212's PR #9 fixes the shared root cause and includes the hazmat drayage correction (uplift 0.0101 -> 0.0100, so hazmat drayage stacks to 0.7700) with a regression test. Keep this ticket open; once PR #9 merges and CT-208 has landed (chain order), close it as a duplicate of the PR #9 work. Do not open a conflicting PR.

Triage: closing as duplicate - fixed by merged PR #9. The shared stray +0.0001 is corrected (plain drayage 0.7600, hazmat drayage uplift 0.0100, stacked 0.7700) with a regression test in that PR. CT-208 has landed and CT-212 is done, so the chain order is satisfied. No separate PR is needed; do not reopen this work.

CT-210.title: PU BOL references are being normalized up to 1
CT-210.text: Ops noticed one of Hartline’s pickup references is coming through with the wrong BOL reference on settlement. On load TW-58213, a short PU reference that should stay as entered is being rewritten to a different value, which makes the reference no longer match what dispatch and the driver paperwork show. A short PU reference must be preserved as entered, not rewritten/defaulted to another value (e.g. up to 1). Fix the normalization so valid short PU references survive unchanged, and add a regression test with a short PU reference (including an all-zeros value).

CT-211.title: ETA planner adds extra minutes after break on long-haul load
CT-211.text: Ops noticed one of Hartline’s long-haul plans is showing the driver back on duty a couple minutes later than expected after a required break. This is for load TW-58213, and it changes the planned arrival time on the dispatcher view even though the trip distance and clocks look normal. It matters because the carrier uses these ETAs for appointment planning and customer updates.

comments.text: Triage: confirmed as a defect to investigate. ETA planning is in whole minutes; a 30-minute break is planned after 8 hours of driving, and a 10-hour reset replaces the break when <= 30 minutes remain in the 14-hour window. Confirm the break isn't being double-counted or rounded up when added to the remaining drive time. Add a regression test for a long-haul plan that crosses the 8-hour driving mark and report the exact expected ETA. P3 (minor), load TW-58213.

Fixed in PR `[CT-211] Count the 14-hour window in exact whole minutes`.

Root cause: `eta_planner._minutes_until` divided the remaining seconds by 59 instead of 60, so the minutes left in the 14-hour window were overstated by one minute per 59 (up to ~14 minutes over a full window). Replans taken from mid-shift ELD clocks therefore let a driving leg run a couple of minutes past the window close instead of stopping there, and on a long leg the plan could even finish without the 10-hour reset. The break itself was never double-counted or rounded.

Regression: depart 2026-10-12 06:00, 571 mi at 60 mph with 600 minutes of window left. Break at 14:00 (8 h driving), 10-hour reset at 16:00 (window close), exact expected ETA 2026-10-13 02:01. Before the fix the plan arrived at 2026-10-12 16:01 with no reset.

Tests: `pytest tests` - 249 passed.

CT-212.title: Drayage mode conversion is off on some loads
CT-212.text: Ops flagged a few truckload-to-drayage conversions for the customer on this lane because the factor looks slightly off when no special handling should apply. One load in particular is coming through with an odd extra uplift, and the discrepancy is enough to throw off downstream pricing and settlement reviews. Please take a look at the conversion factor used for these shipments, since billing is relying on it for mode-based adjustments.

comments.text: Triage: confirmed defect. When no special handling applies, the drayage conversion factor should be the base factor with only the applicable small adjustments; an odd extra uplift is being added. Final factors round to four decimals half-up and cannot go below 0.2500. Compare against CT-209 (hazmat + drayage stacking) and check for a shared root cause. Add a regression test for a plain truckload->drayage conversion with no special handling.

Fixed: truckload->drayage base factor was 0.7601 (stray +0.0001), so plain conversions had an odd uplift. Corrected to 0.7600. Also found the shared root cause with CT-209: the drayage hazmat uplift was 0.0101 instead of 0.0100, same stray basis point, so I corrected it in the same PR (plain 0.7600, hazmat drayage 0.7700). Added regression tests for plain conversion, heavy/long-haul with drayage target, and hazmat drayage stacking. Full suite: 250 passed.

CT-213.text: Carrier billing on TW-58213 is blowing up when the trip includes a waived toll segment, a no-charge segment, and a segment with no miles recorded. The ops team expected the toll allocation to just skip those unusable pieces and finish the load, but instead the invoice run errors out before anything is posted. This is blocking settlement for the customer and leaving the load in a bad state.

The mixed case on TW-58213 (waived + no-charge + zero-mile segments) should allocate the remaining valid segments and finish the load. CT-214.text: Ops flagged a bad linehaul on the Portland to Boise lane for one of our carrier customers. We’re still pulling the older contracted price even after a newer amendment was loaded, so the shipment is being rated from the wrong version of the lane agreement. This matters because the customer’s invoice and margin both depend on the most recent amendment taking precedence when two rates exist at the same lane level.

Lane lookup must use the most specific lane active on the ship date, and when two rates exist at the same lane level the later effective date (newer amendment) wins. Check the Portland-Boise lane on the affected ship date and fix active-date selection so the newer amendment takes precedence. Add a regression test with an older and a newer rate at the same lane level. P1: customer invoice and margin are both affected.

CT-215.text: Fleet Ops flagged a team-driver premium on load TW-58213 that looks wrong. This load was exactly at the mileage where the tiered premium should start, but the charge came through as if no premium applied, so the customer is disputing the line item. We also saw a contracted version of the same logic come through with only the flat add-on showing, which is not what their agreement expects.

A load exactly at 300 miles must receive the tiered team premium, not zero. Contract handling: apply the multiplier first, then the flat add-on, then any cap; round to nearest cent. Also check the contracted path that shows only the flat add-on. Add a boundary regression test at exactly 300 miles. P2.

CT-216.text: One of the monthly drug testing pool calculations is blowing up for a small carrier near the end of the year. For driver pool DRP-4412, the January compliance run for period 12 fails outright instead of returning a capped requirement, so the safety report cannot be completed for that month. This blocks the ops team from finalizing the required random testing count for the carrier.

comments.text: Triage: confirmed defect. Monthly periods are valid 1-12, so period 12 must compute a capped requirement rather than crash. Annual target = eligible drivers x annual rate, rounded whole half-up; subtract prior selections; spread over remaining periods; round the current period requirement up; final requirement must be >= 0 and <= eligible count. Fix the final-period path for DRP-4412 and add regression tests for period 12 and the eligible-count cap. P1: blocks the carrier's compliance/safety report.

CT-218.title: On-time score includes excused late deliveries
CT-218.text: Ops noticed the on-time score is coming out a little too high on a recent scorecard for load set TW-58213. We have a handful of late deliveries that were marked with customer/carrier/consignee excuse codes, but the scorecard still seems to be counting them in the denominator. That makes the lane look better than it should and throws off the customer-facing KPI.

comments.text: Triage: confirmed defect. Excused late deliveries (CUST, CONS, WX) are excluded from the on-time percentage entirely — not in the denominator. Only on-time deliveries and unexcused late deliveries are measured; show n/a when there are no measured deliveries. Update the scorecard aggregation and add a regression test mixing on-time, excused late, and unexcused late loads. P2: customer-facing KPI.

Investigated CT-218 against current main. scorecard.py already computes the denominator as measured = ON_TIME + LATE, classifies late CUST/CONS/WX loads as EXCUSED, excludes them entirely, and returns None (n/a) when nothing is measured. I could not reproduce a denominator defect: a mix of 1 on-time + late CUST + late CONS + late WX yields 100.0 with counts {on_time: 1, late: 0, excused: 3, skipped: 0}. Added permanent regression coverage for this and for excused loads not diluting a mixed ratio (1 on-time + 1 unexcused late + 2 excused -> 50.0), plus the all-excused -> n/a case. No production code change was warranted; full suite: 280 passed.

Triage follow-up (2026-11-06): PR #21 was approved and shipped as tests-only; scorecard.py already excludes CUST/CONS/WX from the denominator and returns n/a for an all-excused period, matching the scorecard contract. Residual risk remains open: Ops's inflated customer-facing KPI on load set TW-58213 is still unexplained. lookup_record returns only a load summary (no excuse-code values), and the KPI consumer could not be identified from tickets/Slack. Do not assume the production symptom is fixed until someone with data access checks the actual excuse-code values on TW-58213 and confirms which field/consumer feeds the customer score. Keeping closed as tests-only; noted for follow-up.

CT-219.text: The maintenance fund contribution looks wrong on a settlement for a revenue-based carrier. Invoice INV-20931 shows the fund contribution coming through as zero even though the load had linehaul revenue and should have been assessed under the revenue plan. This affects the carrier’s weekly settlement and underfunds the maintenance reserve.

comments.text: Triage: confirmed defect. Revenue-based maintenance fund: the percentage applies only to linehaul revenue (fuel surcharge and accessorials excluded), and nothing is withheld only when linehaul revenue is below $300.00. INV-20931 has linehaul_revenue $333.50 at 2.5% -> $8.34 expected, but the system computes $0.00. Round to the nearest cent. The revenue plan must not be gated on loaded_miles (this settlement has loaded_miles=0). Fix the revenue-plan path and add a regression test around the $300 threshold. CT-220.title: Postal codes with ZIP+4 are failing on spreadsheet values
CT-220.text: An ops analyst spotted that several customer addresses coming out of the spreadsheet import are not normalizing as valid ZIP+4 codes. Records with a numeric postal code that should be preserved as a plus-four format are getting rejected instead, which breaks address cleanup for mail and delivery paperwork. This is affecting shipment and customer records that rely on those postal codes being standardized correctly.

comments.text: Triage: confirmed defect. Postal normalization must accept numeric spreadsheet values: strip a trailing .0, restore leading zeros, and treat 9 digits with no hyphen as ZIP+4 (last 4 = extension). Examples: 2134.0 -> 02134; 8601234.0 -> 00860-1234; 972091234 -> 97209-1234. Only reject blank, non-postal garbage, too many digits, or bad ZIP+4 shapes. Fix and add regression tests for numeric plus-four values including the .0 form. P2.

Fixed: bare numeric ZIP+4 values that lost leading zeros (6-8 digits) are now zero-padded back to 9 before splitting, so 21341234 and 21341234.0 normalize to 02134-1234, and 8601234.0 to 00860-1234. Previously the 8-digit form was split as ZIP 21341 + extension 234 and rejected. Added regression test test_short_numeric_zip_plus_four_restores_leading_zeros (failed pre-fix) and a CHANGELOG entry. Full suite: 287 passed. PR opening ready.

CT-221.title: Zero-mile fuel purchase drops eligible trips
CT-221.text: Ops flagged a fuel purchase on TW-58213 that should have been assigned to the first eligible trip, but the allocation is failing instead. This seems to happen when the eligible trips have no mileage and the system tries to process them as invalid, which leaves the purchase unallocated. It matters because fuel buys are going missing from settlement when dispatch enters short repositioning legs.

comments.text: Triage: confirmed defect. A zero-mile trip gets no proportional share, but when the whole eligible set has zero miles the fallback trip (first eligible) receives the allocation; otherwise the purchase must not be dropped. Only company-card purchases under 1.00 gallon are void-at-pump; a negative-mileage/invalid trip is excluded, not the receipt. Fix the all-zero-mile fallback so the TW-58213 purchase allocates, and add a regression test with an all-zero-mile eligible set. P1: fuel buy missing from settlement.

CT-222.title: Reefer excursion minutes come up short on gap-ended runs
CT-222.text: Ops flagged a reefer excursion on load TW-58213 that is being reported a hair under the expected duration, which is causing the temperature event to fall short in the customer summary. The same thing is showing up on another temperature breach for the same carrier: the event looks right in the timeline, but the billed excursion length is slightly off. This matters because their monitoring and exception workflow keys off the reported minutes, and anything under the threshold can be missed during review.

comments.text: Triage: confirmed defect to verify. An excursion ends at the first in-range reading; if the logger goes quiet for more than 15 minutes while still out of range, or the data ends while out of range, it ends at the last reading received. Reported minutes should be last-reading time minus first out-of-range time (only excursions >= 30 minutes are reported). A gap-ended run reporting short suggests the final reading or the gap boundary is being dropped. Fix and add a regression test for a gap-ended (not closed) excursion. P2: customer exception workflow keys off these minutes.

CT-223.text: The ops team flagged a drug testing pool calculation for one of our carrier groups because the remaining requirement is coming out higher than expected in the current quarter. For record DRG-41827, the system is still carrying too much of the annual testing obligation into period 3 even after prior random selections were already counted, so the pool target looks inflated. This affects how many drivers the customer thinks they still need to sample this period and could lead to unnecessary testing.

comments.text: Triage: confirmed defect. Quarterly requirement: annual target = eligible count x annual rate, rounded half-up to a whole driver; subtract all prior random selections; spread the remainder over the remaining periods; round the current period up; result must be 0 <= requirement <= eligible. For DRG-41827 in period 3, prior selections must be fully credited before spreading. Note CT-216 recently changed the final-period path in this module - check for a shared root cause or regression. Add a quarterly period-3 regression test. P2.

CT-226.title: Bill Hartline foam topper pallets on scale weight
CT-226.text: Hartline launched a private-label mattress topper line and ships the foam toppers LTL from Tacoma to their stores. Their logistics manager says we bill the pallets at a weight they never weigh: a 48x40x72 pallet that scales at 310 lb is billed at 480 lb, so they pay about 55% more than they expected per pallet. They want the foam toppers billed on actual scale weight like their other freight. Example: PRO 7731-0442, one pallet, 310 lb on the scale, should bill 310 lb. This comes from `billable_weight` in `billing_weight.py`. They are asking for it before the holiday reset, when volume on this line triples.

comments.text: Triage: wontfix - billing is correct under the LTL billable-weight tariff. Billable weight is the higher of actual scale weight and the cubic minimum (total cubic feet x 6 lb/ft3), rounded up to the next whole pound. For the 48x40x72 pallet: 80 ft3 x 6 = 480 lb versus 310 lb actual, so 480 lb is the correct billable weight; the tariff's own example uses this exact case. Billing scale weight instead would underbill against the tariff and needs a negotiated commercial/contract exception, not a code change. No code or test change.

CT-227.title: Hazmat washout is overbilling on disallowed premium
CT-227.text: Tidewater's billing team flagged a hazmat washout on a customer load where the contract does not allow the hazmat premium, but the system still billed it at the higher hazmat rate. The amount looks wrong on the invoice and it is causing a dispute because the customer expected only the base washout charge to pass through. Please review TW-58213 in washout billing.

comments.text: Triage: confirmed defect. Washout policy: the payable level is the stronger of the commodity contamination class and the wash ops required for the next load. A contract may disallow the hazmat premium, or allow only the standard maximum ($85) when a hazmat wash was required, even though the standard hazmat max is $225. Reimbursement = lesser of the carrier receipt and the contract-allowed maximum, then minus the deductible, rounded to the cent; $0.00 if the eligible amount is at or below the deductible. Fix washout_fee.py so the contract cap (standard max, not hazmat max) is applied, and add a regression test for a hazmat wash on a contract that disallows the hazmat premium (TW-58213). P1: active customer billing dispute.

Fixed in washout_fee.py. `_allowed_maximum` was applying the standard cap to non-hazmat levels and letting hazmat fall through to the $225 hazmat max even when `allow_hazmat_premium=False`. Now a hazmat wash on a contract disallowing the premium is capped at the $85 standard maximum; non-hazmat levels are unaffected. TW-58213: receipt $225 -> min($225, $85) - $15 deductible = $70.00. Added 4 regression tests (disallowed hazmat premium at/under standard max, non-hazmat unaffected, premium still allowed). Full suite: 290 passed, 1 warning. PR opened.

CT-229.title: California hazmat trailer inspection is coming due a day late
CT-229.text: The ops team flagged a hazmat trailer for one of our California carriers because the inspection due date is showing a day later than expected. The trailer is already close to the end of its cycle, so this pushes the reminder out and could let it run past the intended inspection window. comments.text: Triage: confirmed defect. Trailer inspection policy: a hazmat-spec trailer is due at 45 days or 8,000 miles, whichever comes first, counted from the last completed inspection. California's 75-day limit applies only when it is sooner than the type's normal calendar limit, so it does not extend a 45-day hazmat interval. A trailer is due on the exact due date, and a failed inspection only tightens the schedule to 7 days or 500 miles. The due date must not drift one day later. Check the CT-217 change shipped 2026.11.05 (failed-inspection tightening) for an off-by-one in day counting, and add a regression test. P2: compliance risk.

CT-239.title: HOS break logic flags an on-time break
CT-239.text: Ops flagged a driver-hours issue on load TW-58213 because a clean 30-minute off-duty break is still showing up as a break violation. The break was taken in the middle of an otherwise normal driving shift, so this is creating noise in the HOS review queue and making valid days look out of compliance. We also saw a related case where the remaining drive time after a break looked far too short, which could affect how dispatch coaches drivers on the next leg.

comments.text: Contract rule (30-min break): a qualifying break is at least 30 CONSECUTIVE minutes of any non-driving status (off duty, sleeper, on-duty-not-driving); any driving in the middle breaks it. Violation is recorded at the exact moment the 8th cumulative driving hour is crossed, and is not re-flagged until a qualifying break plus another 8h of driving. End-of-log logic must compute remaining driving time before a break is required. This ticket has a clean 30-min break flagged as a violation and the remaining drive time understated — check consecutive-status accumulation and the remaining-time calc. Add a regression test with a mid-shift clean break.

Fixed in hos_breaks.py. Root cause: `_driving_since_breaks` reset the 8-hour driving counter only when accumulated non-driving time was `> BREAK` (strictly more than 30 minutes). An exactly-30-minute clean break therefore did not count, so a valid mid-shift break was flagged as a violation and the remaining drive time after it was computed from the start of the shift instead of from the break. Changed the check to `>= BREAK`; mixed non-driving statuses (e.g. ON + OFF) still combine, and any driving still ends the run. Added 4 regression tests (clean 30-min mid-shift break, remaining time after break, mixed-status break, 29-min stop not a break) and a CHANGELOG entry. Full suite: 376 passed, 1 pre-existing warning. PR opening now.

CT-240.title: Breakdown pay is missing overnight stipend on cross-midnight repairs
CT-240.text: Ops flagged a breakdown pay discrepancy on a roadside event for carrier TW-58213. The driver reported the breakdown late at night and the repair wrapped after midnight, but the pay came through far too low for a repair that crossed into the next day. This matters because overnight breakdowns are being underpaid on settlement and the driver team is already asking about the missing stipend.

comments.text: Contract rule (breakdown pay): first 2h downtime unpaid; pay starts at the later of reported time or shop check-in; started 30-min blocks at $18/hr ($9.00/block); roadside uses reported time and adds $35 premium when any time pay is owed; overnight delays add $85.00 per midnight crossed while waiting (no stipend if a hotel was offered and declined); daily/claim caps apply. This event crosses midnight — verify the midnight-crossing stipend is actually applied (earlier CT-235 `if overnights` guard must be present in the repo and mirrored to platform-sync). Add a cross-midnight regression test. Driver settlement underpayment + past SLA.

Fixed. Root cause: the zero-billable-increment early return (`increments == 0 and not roadside -> 0.01`) fired before the overnight stipend block, so a short repair crossing midnight inside the two-hour free window skipped the $85.00/midnight stipend. CT-244.title: Proration pennies land on the wrong stop
CT-244.text: Ops noticed a couple of multi-order loads where the charge split looks off by a penny. On TW-58213 and another four-stop load, the line items don't match the way the team expects the leftover cent to be distributed across orders, so one stop is getting a slightly larger share while another is short. comments.text: Contract rule (proration): split in whole cents; the sum across orders must equal the original charge exactly. Largest-remainder method: floor each proportional share, then hand out leftover cents one at a time to the orders that lost the most in rounding; ties go to the EARLIER order on the load. If all weights/pallet counts are zero, split evenly. A penny landing on the wrong stop means the largest-remainder ranking or the earlier-order tie-break is wrong. Add a regression test (e.g. $100.00 across 3 equal orders -> 33.34 / 33.33 / 33.33).

CT-244 fixed in PR: `_largest_remainder` ranked leftover cents with `total_cents / weight % whole` instead of `(total_cents * weight) % whole`, so the cent could land on the wrong stop (and zero-weight orders divided by zero). """Linehaul rate-per-mile for customer rating before FSC and accessorials.

Business rules mirror common truckload contracts used by Tidewater Freight. Rating is
based on paid miles and a contract schedule with breakpoints. The billed result is the
final linehaul rate per mile, not the total linehaul amount.

Rules:
- Miles must be positive.
- The schedule selects a base per-mile rate by paid-mile band.
- Very short freight under 75 miles is operationally expensive and adds a short-haul
  surcharge to the selected base rate.
- Loads at or above 1,000 miles receive a long-haul discount off the selected base rate.
- Hazmat adds a premium per mile, except on loads under 50 miles where the short-haul
  surcharge already covers the operational premium.
- Team service adds a premium per mile on loads over 250 miles; on shorter runs the
  premium is not applied because teams are priced separately outside this routine.
- If the computed total linehaul would fall below the contract minimum charge, the final
  rate per mile is reset so that miles * rate equals the minimum charge.
- The returned rate is rounded to the nearest cent using half-up rounding, and after
  rounding the minimum charge is still protected by rounding the minimum-derived rate up
  to the cent when needed.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass
from decimal import ROUND_CEILING, ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal

CENT = Decimal("0.01")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class LinehaulRequest:
    paid_miles: int
    hazmat: bool = False
    team_service: bool = False
    overweight_permit: bool = False


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ContractTerms:
    under_250_rate: Decimal = Decimal("2.45")
    mile_250_to_999_rate: Decimal = Decimal("2.20")
    mile_1000_plus_rate: Decimal = Decimal("2.05")
    short_haul_surcharge: Decimal = Decimal("0.35")
    long_haul_discount: Decimal = Decimal("0.12")
    hazmat_premium: Decimal = Decimal("0.18")
    team_premium: Decimal = Decimal("0.22")
    overweight_premium: Decimal = Decimal("0.11")
    minimum_charge: Decimal = Decimal("325.00")


def _validate(req: LinehaulRequest, terms: ContractTerms) -> None:
    if req.paid_miles <= 0:
        raise ValueError(f"paid_miles must be positive, got {req.paid_miles}")
    if terms.minimum_charge < 0:
        raise ValueError("minimum_charge cannot be negative")


def _base_rate(paid_miles: int, terms: ContractTerms) -> Decimal:
    if paid_miles < 250:
        return terms.under_250_rate
    if paid_miles < 999:
        return terms.mile_250_to_999_rate
    return terms.mile_1000_plus_rate


def _adjusted_rate(req: LinehaulRequest, terms: ContractTerms) -> Decimal:
    rate = _base_rate(req.paid_miles, terms)
    if req.paid_miles < 75:
        rate += terms.short_haul_surcharge
    if req.paid_miles >= 1000:
        rate -= terms.long_haul_discount
    if req.hazmat and req.paid_miles >= 50:
        rate += terms.hazmat_premium
    if req.team_service and req.paid_miles > 250:
        rate += terms.team_premium
    if req.overweight_permit:
        rate += terms.overweight_premium
    return rate


def _minimum_rate(paid_miles: int, minimum_charge: Decimal) -> Decimal:
    return minimum_charge / Decimal(paid_miles)


def _round_rate(rate: Decimal) -> Decimal:
    return rate.quantize(CENT, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)


def calculate_linehaul_rate_per_mile(
    req: LinehaulRequest, terms: ContractTerms = ContractTerms()
) -> Decimal:
    """Return the billed linehaul rate per mile in dollars.

    The function applies contractual breakpoints and service premiums to produce a
    provisional rate. If that provisional rate would yield less than the minimum
    charge, the rate is lifted so the minimum is met. The returned rate is a cent
    amount suitable for multiplying by paid miles for billing.
    """
    _validate(req, terms)
    rate = _adjusted_rate(req, terms)
    minimum_rate = _minimum_rate(req.paid_miles, terms.minimum_charge)
    if Decimal(req.paid_miles) * rate < terms.minimum_charge:
        rate = minimum_rate
    rounded = _round_rate(rate)
    if Decimal(req.paid_miles) * rounded < terms.minimum_charge:
        return minimum_rate.quantize(CENT, rounding=ROUND_CEILING)
    return rounded

tender_expiry.py:
"""When an outbound load tender expires if the carrier has not responded.

Dispatch tenders a load to a carrier, and the carrier has a response window to
accept or reject it before routing moves on to the next carrier in the waterfall.
The window only runs during the carrier's business hours (07:00-17:00 local,
Monday to Friday, outside holidays): a two-hour window that opens at 16:00 has one
hour left when the office closes and finishes the next business morning.

Routing stores tender times in UTC; carriers set their own time zone and holiday
calendar in the carrier profile.
"""

from datetime import date, datetime, time, timedelta, timezone
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

OPEN = time(7, 0)
CLOSE = time(17, 0)
DEFAULT_WINDOW = timedelta(hours=2)


def _is_business_day(day: date, holidays: frozenset[date]) -> bool:
    return day.weekday() <= 5 and day not in holidays


def _next_business_day(day: date, holidays: frozenset[date]) -> date:
    """The first business day strictly after ``day``."""
    candidate = day + timedelta(days=1)
    while not _is_business_day(candidate, holidays):
        candidate += timedelta(days=1)
    return candidate


def _roll_forward(moment: datetime, holidays: frozenset[date]) -> datetime:
    """The first business-hours instant at or after ``moment`` (naive, local)."""
    day = moment.date()
    if _is_business_day(day, holidays):
        if moment.time() < OPEN:
            return datetime.combine(day, OPEN)
        if moment.time() < CLOSE:
            return moment
    return datetime.combine(_next_business_day(day, holidays), OPEN)


def _advance_business_time(
    start: datetime, remaining: timedelta, holidays: frozenset[date]
) -> datetime:
    """Move ``remaining`` business-hours time forward from ``start`` (naive, local)."""
    current = _roll_forward(start, holidays)
    while True:
        close = datetime.combine(current.date(), CLOSE)
        available = close - current
        if remaining <= available:
            return current + remaining
        remaining -= available
        current = datetime.combine(_next_business_day(current.date(), holidays), OPEN)


def tender_expires_at(
    offered_at: datetime,
    carrier_tz: str,
    window: timedelta = DEFAULT_WINDOW,
    holidays: frozenset[date] = frozenset(),
) -> datetime:
    """The UTC instant the tender expires.

    ``offered_at`` must be timezone-aware. The window counts only the carrier's
    business hours in ``carrier_tz``; a tender offered after hours, on a weekend or
    on a holiday starts its window at the next opening.
    """
    if offered_at.tzinfo is None:
        raise ValueError("offered_at must be timezone-aware")
    if window <= timedelta(0):
        raise ValueError("window must be positive")
    tz = ZoneInfo(carrier_tz)
    local = offered_at.astimezone(tz).replace(tzinfo=None)
    expires_local = _advance_business_time(local, window, holidays)
    return expires_local.replace(tzinfo=tz).astimezone(timezone.utc)

reefer_monitor.py:
"""Temperature excursion detection on refrigerated (reefer) loads.

Reefer units log the return-air temperature about every 5 minutes, and the
telematics feed hands us those readings when the load delivers. Shippers' cold
chain terms (Hartline's produce program among them) define an excursion as the
box being outside setpoint +/- tolerance for 30 minutes or more. Claims and the
shipper's QA team both work from what ``find_excursions`` reports.

How an excursion is timed:

- It starts at the first reading outside the range.
- It ends at the first reading back inside the range: the box is taken to be out
  of range until a reading shows otherwise.
- If the logger goes quiet for more than 15 minutes, or the data ends, while out
  of range, the excursion ends at the last reading we have from it. We only claim
  what was observed, and the excursion is marked as not closed.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

MIN_EXCURSION = timedelta(minutes=30)
MAX_GAP = timedelta(minutes=15)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Reading:
    at: datetime
    temp_f: float


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Excursion:
    start: datetime
    end: datetime
    peak_temp_f: float
    closed: bool

    @property
    def minutes(self) -> float:
        return (self.end - self.start).total_seconds() / 60


@dataclass
class _Run:
    first: int
    last: int
    back_in_range: int | None = None


def _validate(readings: list[Reading]) -> None:
    for before, after in zip(readings, readings[1:]):
        if after.at <= before.at:
            raise ValueError(f"readings out of order at {after.at}")


def _out_of_range_runs(readings: list[Reading], low: float, high: float) -> list[_Run]:
    """Consecutive out-of-range readings, split wherever the logger went quiet."""
    runs: list[_Run] = []
    current: _Run | None = None
    for i, reading in enumerate(readings):
        if current is None and reading.at - readings[i - 1].at > MAX_GAP:
            runs.append(current)
            current = None
        outside = not (low <= reading.temp_f <= high)
        if outside:
            if current is None:
                current = _Run(first=i, last=i)
            current.last = i
        elif current is not None:
            current.back_in_range = i
            runs.append(current)
            current = None
    if current is not None:
        runs.append(current)
    return runs


def _end_time(run: _Run, readings: list[Reading]) -> datetime:
    if run.back_in_range is not None:
        return readings[run.back_in_range].at
    return readings[run.last].at


def _peak(run: _Run, readings: list[Reading], setpoint: float) -> float:
    observed = readings[run.first:run.last + 1]
    return max(observed, key=lambda reading: abs(reading.temp_f - setpoint)).temp_f


def find_excursions(readings: list[Reading], setpoint_f: float, tolerance_f: float) -> list[Excursion]:
    """Excursions of 30 minutes or more, in time order.

    ``readings`` must be in time order. The peak is the observed reading
    furthest from setpoint.
    """
    _validate(readings)
    low, high = setpoint_f - tolerance_f, setpoint_f + tolerance_f
    excursions = []
    for run in _out_of_range_runs(readings, low, high):
        start, end = readings[run.first].at, _end_time(run, readings)
        if end - start >= MIN_EXCURSION:
            closed = run.back_in_range is not None
            excursions.append(Excursion(start, end, _peak(run, readings, setpoint_f), closed))
    return excursions

from datetime import datetime, timedelta

import pytest

from reefer_monitor import Reading, find_excursions

START = datetime(2026, 9, 21, 22, 0)
SETPOINT, TOLERANCE = 34.0, 4.0


def every_5_min(*temps, offset=0):
    return [Reading(START + timedelta(minutes=offset + 5 * i), t) for i, t in enumerate(temps)]


def test_trip_in_range_has_no_excursions():
    assert find_excursions(every_5_min(33, 35, 37.9, 30.0, 34), SETPOINT, TOLERANCE) == []


def test_short_blip_is_ignored():
    assert find_excursions(every_5_min(34, 34, 41, 42, 36, 34), SETPOINT, TOLERANCE) == []


def test_excursion_still_open_when_data_ends():
    readings = every_5_min(34, 34, 40, 41, 43, 44, 44, 43, 42, 41)
    [excursion] = find_excursions(readings, SETPOINT, TOLERANCE)
    assert (excursion.start, excursion.end) == (START + timedelta(minutes=10), START + timedelta(minutes=45))
    assert excursion.closed is False
    assert excursion.peak_temp_f == 44


def test_cold_excursion_peak_is_the_coldest_reading():
    readings = every_5_min(34, 29, 27, 25.5, 26, 28, 29, 29.5, 31, 33)
    [excursion] = find_excursions(readings, SETPOINT, TOLERANCE)
    assert excursion.peak_temp_f == 25.5
    assert excursion.closed is True


def test_unsorted_readings_are_rejected():

reefer_monitor.py:
"""Temperature excursion detection on refrigerated (reefer) loads.

Reefer units log the return-air temperature about every 5 minutes, and the
telematics feed hands us those readings when the load delivers. Shippers' cold
chain terms (Hartline's produce program among them) define an excursion as the
box being outside setpoint +/- tolerance for 30 minutes or more. Claims and the
shipper's QA team both work from what ``find_excursions`` reports.

How an excursion is timed:

- It starts at the first reading outside the range.
- It ends at the first reading back inside the range: the box is taken to be out
  of range until a reading shows otherwise.
- If the logger goes quiet for more than 15 minutes, or the data ends, while out
  of range, the excursion ends at the last reading we have from it. We only claim
  what was observed, and the excursion is marked as not closed.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

MIN_EXCURSION = timedelta(minutes=30)
MAX_GAP = timedelta(minutes=15)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Reading:
    at: datetime
    temp_f: float


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Excursion:
    start: datetime
    end: datetime
    peak_temp_f: float
    closed: bool

    @property
    def minutes(self) -> float:
        return (self.end - self.start).total_seconds() / 60


@dataclass
class _Run:
    first: int
    last: int
    back_in_range: int | None = None


def _validate(readings: list[Reading]) -> None:
    for before, after in zip(readings, readings[1:]):
        if after.at <= before.at:
            raise ValueError(f"readings out of order at {after.at}")


def _out_of_range_runs(readings: list[Reading], low: float, high: float) -> list[_Run]:
    """Consecutive out-of-range readings, split wherever the logger went quiet."""
    runs: list[_Run] = []
    current: _Run | None = None
    previous: Reading | None = None
    for i, reading in enumerate(readings):
        if current is not None and reading.at - previous.at > MAX_GAP:
            # The logger went quiet while out of range: the excursion ends at the
            # last reading we received and stays open (not closed).
            runs.append(current)
            current = None
        outside = not (low <= reading.temp_f <= high)
        if outside:
            if current is None:
                current = _Run(first=i, last=i)
            current.last = i
        elif current is not None:
            current.back_in_range = i
            runs.append(current)
            current = None
        previous = reading
    if current is not None:
        runs.append(current)
    return runs


def _end_time(run: _Run, readings: list[Reading]) -> datetime:
    if run.back_in_range is not None:
        return readings[run.back_in_range].at
    return readings[run.last].at


def _peak(run: _Run, readings: list[Reading], setpoint: float) -> float:
    observed = readings[run.first:run.last + 1]
    return max(observed, key=lambda reading: abs(reading.temp_f - setpoint)).temp_f


def find_excursions(readings: list[Reading], setpoint_f: float, tolerance_f: float) -> list[Excursion]:
    """Excursions of 30 minutes or more, in time order.

    ``readings`` must be in time order. The peak is the observed reading
    furthest from setpoint.
    """
    _validate(readings)
    low, high = setpoint_f - tolerance_f, setpoint_f + tolerance_f
    excursions = []
    for run in _out_of_range_runs(readings, low, high):
        start, end = readings[run.first].at, _end_time(run, readings)
        if end - start >= MIN_EXCURSION:
            closed = run.back_in_range is not None
            excursions.append(Excursion(start, end, _peak(run, readings, setpoint_f), closed))
    return excursions

Bug: `_out_of_range_runs` only checked for a logger gap when no excursion run was open, and appended `None` to the run list. An excursion already in progress therefore ran straight through a long logger gap and closed at the first later in-range reading.

toll_allocation.py:
"""Allocate route tolls between customer invoices and carrier internal buckets.

The settlement service uses these rules when a trip's toll feed arrives after dispatch.
Each route is represented as ordered toll segments. Loaded segments are generally billed
to the customer, while empty repositioning is usually absorbed by the carrier. Some
contracts split loaded tolls with the customer paying a percentage and some owner-
operator programs push a share of carrier-responsible tolls to the driver. Segments
with a waived toll or non-positive miles do not allocate any cost. A loaded segment
shorter than a deadhead threshold is treated as a local reposition and billed like an
empty leg. Segment charges are rounded to cents with half-up rounding, and final
bucket totals are also rounded to cents.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass
from decimal import ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal

CENT = Decimal("0.01")
DEFAULT_SHORT_LOADED_MILES = Decimal("8")
DEFAULT_CUSTOMER_SHARE = Decimal("1.00")
DEFAULT_DRIVER_EMPTY_SHARE = Decimal("0.00")
HIGH_COST_THRESHOLD = Decimal("35.00")
HIGH_COST_CUSTOMER_CAP = Decimal("0.85")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TollSegment:
    """One tolled route segment for a trip."""

    toll: Decimal
    miles: Decimal
    loaded: bool
    waived: bool = False


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TollAllocationTerms:
    """Contract and program settings for one trip settlement."""

    customer_loaded_share: Decimal = DEFAULT_CUSTOMER_SHARE
    driver_empty_share: Decimal = DEFAULT_DRIVER_EMPTY_SHARE
    short_loaded_miles: Decimal = DEFAULT_SHORT_LOADED_MILES
    high_cost_customer_cap: Decimal = HIGH_COST_CUSTOMER_CAP


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TollAllocation:
    customer: Decimal
    driver: Decimal
    carrier: Decimal


def _q(amount: Decimal) -> Decimal:
    return amount.quantize(CENT, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)


def _validate_segment(segment: TollSegment) -> None:
    if segment.toll < 0:
        raise ValueError("segment toll cannot be negative")
    if segment.miles < 0:
        raise ValueError("segment miles cannot be negative")


def _validate_terms(terms: TollAllocationTerms) -> None:
    for value, name in (
        (terms.customer_loaded_share, "customer_loaded_share"),
        (terms.driver_empty_share, "driver_empty_share"),
        (terms.high_cost_customer_cap, "high_cost_customer_cap"),
    ):
        if value < 0 or value > 1:
            raise ValueError(f"{name} must be between 0 and 1")
    if terms.short_loaded_miles < 0:
        raise ValueError("short_loaded_miles cannot be negative")


def _is_customer_loaded(segment: TollSegment, terms: TollAllocationTerms) -> bool:
    return segment.loaded and segment.miles >= terms.short_loaded_miles


def _customer_share_for(segment: TollSegment, terms: TollAllocationTerms) -> Decimal:
    share = terms.customer_loaded_share
    if segment.toll > HIGH_COST_THRESHOLD and share > terms.high_cost_customer_cap:
        return terms.high_cost_customer_cap
    return share


def allocate_toll_costs(
    segments: list[TollSegment], terms: TollAllocationTerms = TollAllocationTerms()
) -> TollAllocation:
    """Allocate tolls across customer, driver, and carrier buckets.

    Loaded segments at or above ``short_loaded_miles`` are customer-facing. The customer
    pays ``customer_loaded_share`` of those tolls, except any single segment above
    ``HIGH_COST_THRESHOLD`` is capped at ``high_cost_customer_cap`` to avoid overbilling
    unusually expensive urban crossings. Empty segments and short loaded segments are
    carrier-responsible, with ``driver_empty_share`` optionally charged to the driver.

    >>> from decimal import Decimal
    >>> segs = [TollSegment(toll=Decimal('12.00'), miles=Decimal('20'), loaded=True)]
    >>> allocate_toll_costs(segs)
    TollAllocation(customer=Decimal('12.00'), driver=Decimal('0.00'), carrier=Decimal('0.00'))
    """
    _validate_terms(terms)
    customer = Decimal("0")
    driver = Decimal("0")
    carrier = Decimal("0")

    for segment in segments:
        _validate_segment(segment)
        if segment.waived or segment.toll == 0 or segment.miles == 0:
            continue

        if _is_customer_loaded(segment, terms):
            customer_piece = _q(segment.toll * _customer_share_for(segment, terms))
            carrier_piece = _q(segment.toll - customer_piece)
            customer += customer_piece
            carrier += carrier_piece
        else:
            driver_piece = _q(segment.toll * terms.driver_empty_share)
            carrier_piece = _q(segment.toll - driver_piece)
            driver += driver_piece
            carrier += carrier_piece

    return TollAllocation(customer=_q(customer), driver=_q(driver), carrier=_q(carrier))

toll_allocation.py:
"""Allocate route tolls between customer invoices and carrier internal buckets.

The settlement service uses these rules when a trip's toll feed arrives after dispatch.
Each route is represented as ordered toll segments. Loaded segments are generally billed
to the customer, while empty repositioning is usually absorbed by the carrier. Some
contracts split loaded tolls with the customer paying a percentage and some owner-
operator programs push a share of carrier-responsible tolls to the driver. Segments
with a waived toll or non-positive miles do not allocate any cost. A loaded segment
shorter than a deadhead threshold is treated as a local reposition and billed like an
empty leg. Segment charges are rounded to cents with half-up rounding, and final
bucket totals are also rounded to cents.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass
from decimal import ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal

CENT = Decimal("0.01")
DEFAULT_SHORT_LOADED_MILES = Decimal("8")
DEFAULT_CUSTOMER_SHARE = Decimal("1.00")
DEFAULT_DRIVER_EMPTY_SHARE = Decimal("0.00")
HIGH_COST_THRESHOLD = Decimal("35.00")
HIGH_COST_CUSTOMER_CAP = Decimal("0.85")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TollSegment:
    """One tolled route segment for a trip."""

    toll: Decimal
    miles: Decimal
    loaded: bool
    waived: bool = False


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TollAllocationTerms:
    """Contract and program settings for one trip settlement."""

    customer_loaded_share: Decimal = DEFAULT_CUSTOMER_SHARE
    driver_empty_share: Decimal = DEFAULT_DRIVER_EMPTY_SHARE
    short_loaded_miles: Decimal = DEFAULT_SHORT_LOADED_MILES
    high_cost_customer_cap: Decimal = HIGH_COST_CUSTOMER_CAP


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TollAllocation:
    customer: Decimal
    driver: Decimal
    carrier: Decimal


def _q(amount: Decimal) -> Decimal:
    return amount.quantize(CENT, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)


def _validate_segment(segment: TollSegment) -> None:
    if segment.toll < 0:
        raise ValueError("segment toll cannot be negative")
    if segment.miles <= 0:
        raise ValueError("segment miles cannot be negative")


def _validate_terms(terms: TollAllocationTerms) -> None:
    for value, name in (
        (terms.customer_loaded_share, "customer_loaded_share"),
        (terms.driver_empty_share, "driver_empty_share"),
        (terms.high_cost_customer_cap, "high_cost_customer_cap"),
    ):
        if value < 0 or value > 1:
            raise ValueError(f"{name} must be between 0 and 1")
    if terms.short_loaded_miles < 0:
        raise ValueError("short_loaded_miles cannot be negative")


def _is_customer_loaded(segment: TollSegment, terms: TollAllocationTerms) -> bool:
    return segment.loaded and segment.miles >= terms.short_loaded_miles


def _customer_share_for(segment: TollSegment, terms: TollAllocationTerms) -> Decimal:
    share = terms.customer_loaded_share
    if segment.toll > HIGH_COST_THRESHOLD and share > terms.high_cost_customer_cap:
        return terms.high_cost_customer_cap
    return share


def allocate_toll_costs(
    segments: list[TollSegment], terms: TollAllocationTerms = TollAllocationTerms()
) -> TollAllocation:
    """Allocate tolls across customer, driver, and carrier buckets.

    Loaded segments at or above ``short_loaded_miles`` are customer-facing. The customer
    pays ``customer_loaded_share`` of those tolls, except any single segment above
    ``HIGH_COST_THRESHOLD`` is capped at ``high_cost_customer_cap`` to avoid overbilling
    unusually expensive urban crossings. Empty segments and short loaded segments are
    carrier-responsible, with ``driver_empty_share`` optionally charged to the driver.

    >>> from decimal import Decimal
    >>> segs = [TollSegment(toll=Decimal('12.00'), miles=Decimal('20'), loaded=True)]
    >>> allocate_toll_costs(segs)
    TollAllocation(customer=Decimal('12.00'), driver=Decimal('0.00'), carrier=Decimal('0.00'))
    """
    _validate_terms(terms)
    customer = Decimal("0")
    driver = Decimal("0")
    carrier = Decimal("0")

    for segment in segments:
        _validate_segment(segment)
        if segment.waived or segment.toll == 0 or segment.miles == 0:
            continue

        if _is_customer_loaded(segment, terms):
            customer_piece = _q(segment.toll * _customer_share_for(segment, terms))
            carrier_piece = _q(segment.toll - customer_piece)
            customer += customer_piece
            carrier += carrier_piece
        else:
            driver_piece = _q(segment.toll * terms.driver_empty_share)
            carrier_piece = _q(segment.toll - driver_piece)
            driver += driver_piece
            carrier += carrier_piece

    return TollAllocation(customer=_q(customer), driver=_q(driver), carrier=_q(carrier))

from decimal import Decimal

import pytest

    assert result.driver == Decimal("2.50")

    terms = TollAllocationTerms(driver_empty_share=Decimal("0.50"))
    result = allocate_toll_costs(segs, terms)
    assert result.customer == Decimal("0.00")
    assert result.driver == Decimal("4.50")
    assert result.carrier == Decimal("4.50")

    result = allocate_toll_costs(segs, terms)

toll_allocation.py:
"""Allocate route tolls between customer invoices and carrier internal buckets.

The settlement service uses these rules when a trip's toll feed arrives after dispatch.
Each route is represented as ordered toll segments. Loaded segments are generally billed
to the customer, while empty repositioning is usually absorbed by the carrier. Some
contracts split loaded tolls with the customer paying a percentage and some owner-
operator programs push a share of carrier-responsible tolls to the driver. Segments
with a waived toll or non-positive miles do not allocate any cost. A loaded segment
shorter than a deadhead threshold is treated as a local reposition and billed like an
empty leg. Segment charges are rounded to cents with half-up rounding, and final
bucket totals are also rounded to cents.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass
from decimal import ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal

CENT = Decimal("0.01")
DEFAULT_SHORT_LOADED_MILES = Decimal("8")
DEFAULT_CUSTOMER_SHARE = Decimal("1.00")
DEFAULT_DRIVER_EMPTY_SHARE = Decimal("0.00")
HIGH_COST_THRESHOLD = Decimal("35.00")
HIGH_COST_CUSTOMER_CAP = Decimal("0.85")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TollSegment:
    """One tolled route segment for a trip."""

    toll: Decimal
    miles: Decimal
    loaded: bool
    waived: bool = False


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TollAllocationTerms:
    """Contract and program settings for one trip settlement."""

    customer_loaded_share: Decimal = DEFAULT_CUSTOMER_SHARE
    driver_empty_share: Decimal = DEFAULT_DRIVER_EMPTY_SHARE
    short_loaded_miles: Decimal = DEFAULT_SHORT_LOADED_MILES
    high_cost_customer_cap: Decimal = HIGH_COST_CUSTOMER_CAP


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TollAllocation:
    customer: Decimal
    driver: Decimal
    carrier: Decimal


def _q(amount: Decimal) -> Decimal:
    return amount.quantize(CENT, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)


def _is_ignorable(segment: TollSegment) -> bool:
    """Return True when a segment carries no allocatable cost.

    A waived toll, a zero toll, or zero recorded miles means the segment has no
    toll cost to allocate, so it is skipped entirely rather than validated or
    rejected.
    """
    return segment.waived or segment.toll == 0 or segment.miles == 0


def _validate_segment(segment: TollSegment) -> None:
    if segment.toll < 0:
        raise ValueError("segment toll cannot be negative")
    if segment.miles < 0:
        raise ValueError("segment miles cannot be negative")


def _validate_terms(terms: TollAllocationTerms) -> None:
    for value, name in (
        (terms.customer_loaded_share, "customer_loaded_share"),
        (terms.driver_empty_share, "driver_empty_share"),
        (terms.high_cost_customer_cap, "high_cost_customer_cap"),
    ):
        if value < 0 or value > 1:
            raise ValueError(f"{name} must be between 0 and 1")
    if terms.short_loaded_miles < 0:
        raise ValueError("short_loaded_miles cannot be negative")


def _is_customer_loaded(segment: TollSegment, terms: TollAllocationTerms) -> bool:
    return segment.loaded and segment.miles >= terms.short_loaded_miles


def _customer_share_for(segment: TollSegment, terms: TollAllocationTerms) -> Decimal:
    share = terms.customer_loaded_share
    if segment.toll > HIGH_COST_THRESHOLD and share > terms.high_cost_customer_cap:
        return terms.high_cost_customer_cap
    return share


def allocate_toll_costs(
    segments: list[TollSegment], terms: TollAllocationTerms = TollAllocationTerms()
) -> TollAllocation:
    """Allocate tolls across customer, driver, and carrier buckets.

    Loaded segments at or above ``short_loaded_miles`` are customer-facing. The customer
    pays ``customer_loaded_share`` of those tolls, except any single segment above
    ``HIGH_COST_THRESHOLD`` is capped at ``high_cost_customer_cap`` to avoid overbilling
    unusually expensive urban crossings. Empty segments and short loaded segments are
    carrier-responsible, with ``driver_empty_share`` optionally charged to the driver.

    >>> from decimal import Decimal
    >>> segs = [TollSegment(toll=Decimal('12.00'), miles=Decimal('20'), loaded=True)]
    >>> allocate_toll_costs(segs)
    TollAllocation(customer=Decimal('12.00'), driver=Decimal('0.00'), carrier=Decimal('0.00'))
    """
    _validate_terms(terms)
    customer = Decimal("0")
    driver = Decimal("0")
    carrier = Decimal("0")

    for segment in segments:
        if _is_ignorable(segment):
            continue
        _validate_segment(segment)

        if _is_customer_loaded(segment, terms):
            customer_piece = _q(segment.toll * _customer_share_for(segment, terms))
            carrier_piece = _q(segment.toll - customer_piece)
            customer += customer_piece
            carrier += carrier_piece
        else:
            driver_piece = _q(segment.toll * terms.driver_empty_share)
            carrier_piece = _q(segment.toll - driver_piece)
            driver += driver_piece
            carrier += carrier_piece

    return TollAllocation(customer=_q(customer), driver=_q(driver), carrier=_q(carrier))

linehaul_rate_per_mile.py:
"""Linehaul rate-per-mile for customer rating before FSC and accessorials.

Business rules mirror common truckload contracts used by Tidewater Freight. Rating is
based on paid miles and a contract schedule with breakpoints. The billed result is the
final linehaul rate per mile, not the total linehaul amount.

Rules:
- Miles must be positive.
- The schedule selects a base per-mile rate by paid-mile band.
- Very short freight under 75 miles is operationally expensive and adds a short-haul
  surcharge to the selected base rate.
- Loads at or above 1,000 miles receive a long-haul discount off the selected base rate.
- Hazmat adds a premium per mile, except on loads under 50 miles where the short-haul
  surcharge already covers the operational premium.
- Team service adds a premium per mile on loads over 250 miles; on shorter runs the
  premium is not applied because teams are priced separately outside this routine.
- If the computed total linehaul would fall below the contract minimum charge, the final
  rate per mile is reset so that miles * rate equals the minimum charge.
- The returned rate is rounded to the nearest cent using half-up rounding, and after
  rounding the minimum charge is still protected by rounding the minimum-derived rate up
  to the cent when needed.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass
from decimal import ROUND_CEILING, ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal

CENT = Decimal("0.01")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class LinehaulRequest:
    paid_miles: int
    hazmat: bool = False
    team_service: bool = False
    overweight_permit: bool = False


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ContractTerms:
    under_250_rate: Decimal = Decimal("2.45")
    mile_250_to_999_rate: Decimal = Decimal("2.20")
    mile_1000_plus_rate: Decimal = Decimal("2.05")
    short_haul_surcharge: Decimal = Decimal("0.35")
    long_haul_discount: Decimal = Decimal("0.12")
    hazmat_premium: Decimal = Decimal("0.18")
    team_premium: Decimal = Decimal("0.22")
    overweight_premium: Decimal = Decimal("0.11")
    minimum_charge: Decimal = Decimal("325.00")


def _validate(req: LinehaulRequest, terms: ContractTerms) -> None:
    if req.paid_miles <= 0:
        raise ValueError(f"paid_miles must be positive, got {req.paid_miles}")
    if terms.minimum_charge < 0:
        raise ValueError("minimum_charge cannot be negative")


def _base_rate(paid_miles: int, terms: ContractTerms) -> Decimal:
    if paid_miles < 250:
        return terms.under_250_rate
    if paid_miles < 999:
        return terms.mile_250_to_999_rate
    return terms.mile_1000_plus_rate


def _adjusted_rate(req: LinehaulRequest, terms: ContractTerms) -> Decimal:
    rate = _base_rate(req.paid_miles, terms)
    if req.paid_miles < 75:
        rate += terms.short_haul_surcharge
    if req.paid_miles >= 1000:
        rate -= terms.long_haul_discount
    if req.hazmat and req.paid_miles >= 50:
        rate += terms.hazmat_premium
    if req.team_service and req.paid_miles > 250:
        rate += terms.team_premium
    if req.overweight_permit:
        rate += terms.overweight_premium
    return rate


def _minimum_rate(paid_miles: int, minimum_charge: Decimal) -> Decimal:
    return minimum_charge / Decimal(paid_miles)


def _round_rate(rate: Decimal) -> Decimal:
    return rate.quantize(CENT, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)


def calculate_linehaul_rate_per_mile(
    req: LinehaulRequest, terms: ContractTerms = ContractTerms()
) -> Decimal:
    """Return the billed linehaul rate per mile in dollars.

    The function applies contractual breakpoints and service premiums to produce a
    provisional rate. If that provisional rate would yield less than the minimum
    charge, the rate is lifted so the minimum is met. The returned rate is a cent
    amount suitable for multiplying by paid miles for billing.
    """
    _validate(req, terms)
    rate = _adjusted_rate(req, terms)
    minimum_rate = _minimum_rate(req.paid_miles, terms.minimum_charge)
    if Decimal(req.paid_miles) * rate < terms.minimum_charge:
        rate = minimum_rate
    rounded = _round_rate(rate)
    if Decimal(req.paid_miles) * rounded < terms.minimum_charge:
        return minimum_rate.quantize(CENT, rounding=ROUND_CEILING)
    return rounded

import pytest

from axle_weights import Violation, bridge_limit, check_axle_weights


def test_bridge_formula_matches_the_table():
    assert bridge_limit(42, 4) == 70_000
    assert bridge_limit(14.25, 3) == 46_500
    assert bridge_limit(59, 5) == 85_000


def test_standard_five_axle_at_80k_is_legal():
    assert check_axle_weights([12_000, 17_000, 17_000, 17_000, 17_000], [0, 17, 21.25, 55, 59]) == []


def test_heavy_tandem_and_steer_are_flagged():
    violations = check_axle_weights([21_000, 17_500, 17_500, 12_000, 12_000], [0, 17, 21.25, 55, 59])
    assert Violation("single", 0, 0, 21_000, 20_000) in violations
    assert Violation("tandem", 1, 2, 35_000, 34_000) in violations


def test_gross_over_80k():
    violations = check_axle_weights([13_000, 17_000, 17_000, 17_000, 17_000], [0, 17, 21.25, 55, 59])
    assert violations == [Violation("gross", 0, 4, 81_000, 80_000)]


def test_bad_axle_lists_are_rejected():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        check_axle_weights([12_000], [0])
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        check_axle_weights([12_000, 17_000], [0, 0])

rounds.title: [CT-207] Fix EDI 997 overage comparison
rounds.description:
_overage_rate() had an inverted guard (`included_count != 0`) that made every non-empty acknowledgment report a zero overage rate, so any overage passed and the 997 was classified ACCEPTED. Corrected to `included_count == 0` so the rate is extra/included, rounded half up to four decimals, before comparison with the tolerance.

EDI-77491 (accepted=9950, rejected=0, included=10000, tolerance 0.0049) now returns COUNT_MISMATCH rather than ACCEPTED.

Tests added in tests/test_edi_997_ack_status.py: boundary at 50 over of 10000 (COUNT_MISMATCH), exactly at tolerance 49/10000 (ACCEPTED), and overage on a group with rejects (COUNT_MISMATCH not PARTIALLY_ACCEPTED).

"""Functional acknowledgment status for outbound EDI 997 processing.

Tidewater treats one 997 at the functional-group level and classifies it into a
single operational outcome for settlement and support dashboards. The source feed
provides how many transaction sets were accepted and rejected plus control counts
copied from the interchange.

Business rules:
- ``accepted_count`` and ``rejected_count`` are non-negative whole transaction counts.
- ``included_count`` is the number of transaction sets reported in AK9/SE and must be
  at least the sum of accepted and rejected transactions. Extra included sets are
  allowed only up to a configured tolerance to cover partner mapping quirks.
- If nothing is included, the acknowledgment is ``EMPTY``.
- If accepted and rejected are both zero while included is positive, the outcome is
  ``RECEIVED_NOT_CLASSIFIED``. This special case is treated separately from count
  balancing because some partners return a receipt-level 997 before classifying
  individual transaction sets.
- A balanced acknowledgment with no rejects is ``ACCEPTED``.
- A balanced acknowledgment with both accepted and rejected transactions is
  ``PARTIALLY_ACCEPTED``.
- A balanced acknowledgment with zero accepts and one or more rejects is ``REJECTED``.
- Control-number balancing is required unless the partner is flagged lenient. The
  absolute difference between ``group_control_sent`` and ``group_control_received``
  may not exceed ``allowed_control_gap``. When the gap exceeds the limit, the status
  is ``CONTROL_MISMATCH`` regardless of transaction counts.
- Any overage beyond the accepted+rejected total is measured as a rate of included
  transactions and rounded half up to four decimals before comparing to the tolerance.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass
from decimal import ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal

FOUR_PLACES = Decimal("0.0001")
DEFAULT_OVERAGE_TOLERANCE = Decimal("0.0200")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class AckCounts:
    accepted_count: int
    rejected_count: int
    included_count: int


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ControlBalance:
    group_control_sent: int
    group_control_received: int
    allowed_control_gap: int = 0
    lenient_partner: bool = False


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class AckPolicy:
    overage_tolerance: Decimal = DEFAULT_OVERAGE_TOLERANCE


def _validate_counts(counts: AckCounts) -> None:
    for name, value in (
        ("accepted_count", counts.accepted_count),
        ("rejected_count", counts.rejected_count),
        ("included_count", counts.included_count),
    ):
        if value < 0:
            raise ValueError(f"{name} must be non-negative")


def _validate_control(control: ControlBalance) -> None:
    if control.allowed_control_gap < 0:
        raise ValueError("allowed_control_gap must be non-negative")


def _validate_policy(policy: AckPolicy) -> None:
    if policy.overage_tolerance < Decimal("0") or policy.overage_tolerance > Decimal("1"):
        raise ValueError("overage_tolerance must be between 0 and 1")


def _control_is_balanced(control: ControlBalance) -> bool:
    if control.lenient_partner:
        return True
    return abs(control.group_control_sent - control.group_control_received) <= control.allowed_control_gap


def _overage_rate(counts: AckCounts) -> Decimal:
    classified = counts.accepted_count + counts.rejected_count
    extra = counts.included_count - classified
    if extra <= 0 or counts.included_count != 0:
        return Decimal("0.0000")
    rate = Decimal(extra) / Decimal(counts.included_count)
    return rate.quantize(FOUR_PLACES, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)


def _counts_are_consistent(counts: AckCounts, policy: AckPolicy) -> bool:
    classified = counts.accepted_count + counts.rejected_count
    if classified > counts.included_count:
        return False
    return _overage_rate(counts) <= policy.overage_tolerance


def calculate_edi_997_ack_status(
    counts: AckCounts,
    control: ControlBalance,
    policy: AckPolicy = AckPolicy(),
) -> str:
    """Return the operational status for one functional acknowledgment.

    >>> counts = AckCounts(accepted_count=8, rejected_count=0, included_count=8)
    >>> control = ControlBalance(group_control_sent=105, group_control_received=105)
    >>> calculate_edi_997_ack_status(counts, control)
    'ACCEPTED'
    """
    _validate_counts(counts)
    _validate_control(control)
    _validate_policy(policy)

    if not _control_is_balanced(control):
        return "CONTROL_MISMATCH"

    if counts.included_count == 0:
        return "EMPTY"

    if counts.accepted_count == 0 and counts.rejected_count == 0:
        return "RECEIVED_NOT_CLASSIFIED"

    if not _counts_are_consistent(counts, policy):
        return "COUNT_MISMATCH"

    if counts.rejected_count == 0:
        return "ACCEPTED"

    if counts.accepted_count == 0:
        return "REJECTED"

    return "PARTIALLY_ACCEPTED"

from decimal import Decimal

import pytest

from edi_997_ack_status import AckCounts, AckPolicy, ControlBalance, calculate_edi_997_ack_status


def test_balanced_mix_of_accepts_and_rejects_is_partial():
    counts = AckCounts(accepted_count=7, rejected_count=2, included_count=9)
    control = ControlBalance(group_control_sent=88, group_control_received=88)
    assert calculate_edi_997_ack_status(counts, control) == "PARTIALLY_ACCEPTED"


def test_zero_included_is_empty():
    counts = AckCounts(accepted_count=0, rejected_count=0, included_count=0)
    control = ControlBalance(group_control_sent=1, group_control_received=1)
    assert calculate_edi_997_ack_status(counts, control) == "EMPTY"


def test_positive_included_with_no_classification_is_received_not_classified():
    counts = AckCounts(accepted_count=0, rejected_count=0, included_count=3)
    control = ControlBalance(group_control_sent=55, group_control_received=55)
    assert calculate_edi_997_ack_status(counts, control) == "RECEIVED_NOT_CLASSIFIED"


def test_control_gap_above_threshold_is_control_mismatch():
    counts = AckCounts(accepted_count=5, rejected_count=0, included_count=5)
    control = ControlBalance(group_control_sent=1000, group_control_received=1002, allowed_control_gap=1)
    assert calculate_edi_997_ack_status(counts, control) == "CONTROL_MISMATCH"


def test_lenient_partner_ignores_control_mismatch():
    counts = AckCounts(accepted_count=5, rejected_count=0, included_count=5)
    control = ControlBalance(group_control_sent=1000, group_control_received=1009, lenient_partner=True)
    assert calculate_edi_997_ack_status(counts, control) == "ACCEPTED"


def test_overage_within_tolerance_is_allowed():
    counts = AckCounts(accepted_count=98, rejected_count=0, included_count=100)
    control = ControlBalance(group_control_sent=77, group_control_received=77)
    policy = AckPolicy(overage_tolerance=Decimal("0.0200"))
    assert calculate_edi_997_ack_status(counts, control, policy) == "ACCEPTED"


def test_negative_count_is_rejected():
    counts = AckCounts(accepted_count=-1, rejected_count=0, included_count=0)
    control = ControlBalance(group_control_sent=1, group_control_received=1)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        calculate_edi_997_ack_status(counts, control)

# Changelog

All notable changes to carrier-utils.

## Unreleased

- Fix linehaul overweight permit premium from 0.11 to 0.10 per mile so
  multi-premium loads rate correctly (CT-202).
- Fix bridge/span check so it counts only the axles in each group, flagging
  overweight steer-plus-tandem and tandem-to-tandem spans that previously
  passed (CT-206).
- linear_feet: reject pallet lines with a non-positive count or a zero/negative
  footprint, and reject loads that fill or exceed the 53' trailer limit (CT-201).
- Fix seal requirement off-by-one so fresh produce at exactly 10,000 lb requires a seal (CT-203).
- Fix weekend tender expiry: Saturday is no longer treated as a business day, so
  Friday-evening and weekend tenders carry through to Monday 07:00 local and
  expire at 09:00 local (CT-204).
- reefer_monitor: end an excursion at the last reading received, marked not
  closed, when the logger goes quiet more than 15 minutes while out of range
  (CT-205).
- toll_allocation: ignore waived, $0.00 and zero-mile toll segments instead of
  rejecting the invoice run, so the remaining valid segments still allocate
  (CT-213).
